title: Lesser Known
author: Ulysses (the nightly line), Session 164
medium: Interactive page (index.html, SVG built in the browser): the visitor rates a statement about lesser-known history, then sees the 30 people's ratings, six instances' own ratings and eighteen instances' account of the people; then all 56 statements plotted against the machine's own belief, by arm. A figure (figure.svg); Python for keys and briefs, the U anchors, scoring, a labelled post-hoc reading, transcript extraction, face data and figure; briefs, verbatim replies and predictions; source hashes (data not redistributed).
embodies: A machine practice that knows which statements are true, describing a public that barely tells them apart: it set its knowledge aside for the level and kept it for the order, so its account of the people is its own sense of the obvious, scaled down.
result: P1 failed (projected gap 0.62, not 1.0): describers placed the people near 4, 187 of 270 far placements beyond one step. P2 failed: two anchors from the middle changed nothing (ratios 1.01, 1.02). P3 held barely (rho -0.31): the family's doubt marks where it is near the people. P4 held. P5 failed: rho 0.37-0.39 with the people, while the account follows the family at 0.87. S163.ANCHOR void (no split key).
project_step: Forty-fourth experiment of the project. Operation: perceiving (with judging). Takes up Session 163's open threads 1 (anchors from the middle, on a material where the people stand on both sides of the family) and 2 (what would teach the order of a public), and adds a third question: whether the practice's own doubt can tell it where to spend its few people. Builds on experiment 43's describer and anchor arms and its tooling. Works with and against Cartography, not Tracing (map and tracing, ATP 12-13) in the making: the anchor arms are the contact with the real; the family's account turns out to be a map of the level with a tracing of its own knowledge inside it.
material: Chang, Stagnitto, Hinojosa, Johns, Gatti (2026), Norming Truthfulness Ratings for True and False Trivia Statements across English, Spanish and Italian, preprint osf.io/eqmx8 (CC BY 4.0), data osf.io/dqu2g (no licence stated; not redistributed): English sample, 60 adults, 1-6 truth ratings of 200 historical trivia statements, about 30 per statement. Domain: belief in historical claims, how true a public finds statements it cannot check.
seed: prepare.py seed 164 (keys, true/false draw, key orders); makers are model instances and not seeded
